decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up right-arm approach to the key; key lies nearer the center and farther forward than the reference.
Continue smooth elbow-up advance while pitching the right gripper downward; keep open and above the table.
Advance toward the visible key with gradual wrist pitch and yaw, preserving joint continuity.
Bring the downward-facing open gripper closer to the key, using the wrist view for final centering.
Translate over the key's lower shaft and finish the downward orientation; leave gripper open for visual alignment.
Fine-center the lower key shaft between the fingers and match its changed in-plane angle.
Close the right fingers on the centered lower shaft; retention will be checked by a subsequent lift.
Maintain full closure, settle the shaft grasp, then begin a slow vertical retention-check lift.
Key remains centered between the closed fingers. Lift clear of the table and start rotating toward the central handover pose.
Raise and yaw the retained key toward the handover area while beginning a continuous elbow-up left-arm receiving approach.
Orient the held key across the central handover gap, and raise the receiving left gripper on its elbow-up path.
Keep the right-hand key stationary and closed while bringing the left gripper inward with a continuous elbow-up rotation.
Lower the receiving left gripper toward the exposed key bow while rotating to a side-on grasp; right hand stays closed and stationary.
Finish the side-facing left approach and reduce its opening before advancing toward the bow. Right grasp remains closed.
Advance the left fingers toward the exposed bow with a partially open gap, keeping both arm bases on their respective sides.
Slow final left-hand advance around the key bow; right hand maintains the shaft grasp until the receiving grip is established.
Close the left fingers around the exposed bow while keeping the right shaft grip secure and stationary.
The bow is visible between the left fingers. Open the right gripper to transfer retention without moving either wrist.
Withdraw the open right hand laterally, checking that the key remains supported by the closed left fingers.
Key is visibly retained by the left hand. Begin turning it upright and lifting toward the keyhole; keep the open right hand clear.
Continue pitching the key toward vertical while lifting enough to keep its tip clear of the tabletop and lock housing.
Replan from the executed prefix with smaller rotations and lifts to satisfy the left joint-continuity guard.
Move toward the visually estimated lock center while smoothly rotating the retained key downward, using smaller continuous increments.
Continue the upright adjustment and approach above the lock, keeping the key tip elevated and the receiving grip closed.
Finish rotating the key to vertical above the lock. Approach height is kept high for wrist-camera slot alignment.
Use the left wrist view to shift toward the slot and align the key's blade with the slot angle before descending.
Correct the yaw direction using the slot's observed rotation in the wrist view; hold height and grip during alignment.
Align the remaining slot yaw and make a shallow descent, keeping the key centered and watching for contact or slip.
Make a slow insertion approach with a small lateral and yaw correction. The long exposed shaft makes seating uncertain, so monitor the next close view.
Pause descent and compensate possible tilt of the key in the bow grasp, rotating about the grasp area with a little clearance.
Hold the adjusted key orientation and make a small planar visual-servo move to bring the slot nearer the projected blade tip.
Descend cautiously while correcting the small projected tip-to-slot offset. Retain the bow with the left fingers fully commanded closed.
The blade now overlaps the slot in the wrist view. Probe downward gently with a millimetric centering correction; seating remains unconfirmed.
Nudge the blade toward the round end of the slot and continue a slow insertion probe without turning yet.
Continue straight down at low speed as the slot stays centered on the blade; watch for the blade to disappear into the opening.
The key shifted relative to the fingers during descent, so stop probing. Lift the bow slightly and compensate its apparent pitch about the grasp before another alignment attempt.
Back the key clear of contact and angle the idle right wrist for an additional view of the shaft and slot alignment.
Keep the held key stationary and improve the second wrist-camera view without crossing arms, to judge its pitch relative to the slot.
The second view suggests the shaft is now close to the lock normal. Approach downward slowly with a small lateral correction, watching both views.
Continue the shallow insertion approach and center the round slot end over the blade tip; do not turn until the shaft seats.
Probe only a few more millimeters with a small centering correction; monitor whether the tip seats or the bow slips further.
The bow has slipped backward rather than seating. Retract to relieve contact, then shift the tip toward the round opening before retrying.
The second view shows the shaft roughly normal to the housing and clear of it. Re-approach vertically with the corrected centering and maintained grip.
The tip now meets the round opening without visible new bow slip. Continue a short straight insertion, holding both orientation and lateral position.
The upper blade is now disappearing into the slot while the bow stays fixed in the grip. Deepen the insertion another short straight segment before turning.
The blade has shortened at the opening and further descent is resisted. Relieve the downward command slightly, then begin a small turn about the slot while holding the bow.
Continue a controlled turn around the slot, keeping insertion height and the closed left grasp steady; the blade remains within the opening.
Continue the turn in small increments with the shaft still at the opening; compensate wrist translation around the slot rather than pulling the key sideways.
The bow shifted relative to the fingers during turning. Stop rotation and slightly reopen to recenter the bow while the slot supports the key.
The bow is no longer between the fingers. Open and lift clear, then straighten the left approach for a fresh grasp of the key supported at the slot.
The released key is leaning at the slot. Bring the open left fingers down over its exposed bow with a straighter downward approach for regrasping.
Center the exposed bow in the open left finger gap using the wrist image, approaching slowly without disturbing the shaft at the slot.
The bow is centered near the left finger contact region. Make a small lateral correction and close around the bow for a steadier regrasp.
Complete closure around the exposed bow, then make a short lift to verify the new grasp before correcting the key's large lean.
Retention is uncertain and the key still appears supported by the slot. Reopen and move the contact region slightly toward the bow before closing again.
Close around the bow now visible in the finger gap, then begin a very small retention-check lift.
The bow is now visibly between the left fingers. Lift the key clear of the slot before correcting its lean.
The key is retained and clear. Rotate its leaning shaft toward vertical about the bow, with a small additional lift for housing clearance.
Continue correcting the visible shaft lean about the retained bow, keeping clearance above the housing and the left arm on its own side.
The regrasp is retained and the shaft is closer to vertical. Translate the tip toward the visible hole with a small clearance lift, without further rotation.
Use the second wrist view to lower the nearly upright shaft toward the hole while correcting its remaining planar offset.
